nodes.title: Try LightGBM XE-NDCG ranking objective
nodes.hypothesis: LightGBM's rank_xendcg objective may optimize top-ranked items more effectively than lambdarank for the nDCG@5 component while retaining within-user grouping.

nodes.title: Increase LightGBM tree capacity
nodes.hypothesis: More leaves can model nonlinear interactions between within-user feedback history, categorical context, and content features, improving ranking discrimination and top-5 ordering.

nodes.title: Add latest-feedback history signals
nodes.hypothesis: Recent feedback is often more predictive than lifetime averages for within-user ranking; exposing the latest feedback per user, video, author, and user-item scope should improve temporal personalization and top-5 ordering.

nodes.title: Reduce leaf minimum for sparse history interactions
nodes.hypothesis: Lowering the minimum samples per leaf lets LightGBM model highly predictive but sparse user-item and recent-feedback history patterns that are suppressed by the current value of 50, improving within-user discrimination and top-5 ranking.

nodes.title: Smooth sparse leaf predictions
nodes.hypothesis: Path smoothing should regularize high-cardinality categorical and user-item history interactions, reducing overfit while preserving useful nonlinear ranking patterns and improving validation GAUC/nDCG.

nodes.title: Broaden ranking gradient context
nodes.hypothesis: Using a truncation level modestly above the evaluation cutoff provides more informative relative-order gradients within each user while still emphasizing the top of the list, potentially improving GAUC without sacrificing nDCG@5.

nodes.title: Focus ranking gradients on top three
nodes.hypothesis: Reducing LightGBM's ranking truncation level from five to three concentrates pairwise optimization on the highest-value positions, which may improve the ordering of the first few items and nDCG@5 without the noisy tail gradients introduced by broader truncation.

nodes.title: Add LightGBM L2 regularization
nodes.hypothesis: Moderate leaf-output shrinkage can reduce overfitting from high-cardinality user/item history features while preserving their ranking signal, improving validation GAUC and nDCG@5.

nodes.title: Strengthen L2 regularization
nodes.hypothesis: Increasing leaf-output shrinkage beyond the current value may further reduce overfitting from high-cardinality user and interaction history features, improving ranking generalization on validation.

nodes.title: Allow more boosting rounds
nodes.hypothesis: The regularized ranker may still be underfit at 400 rounds; increasing the ceiling lets early stopping discover a better iteration count while retaining validation-based stopping to limit overfitting.

nodes.title: Tune L2 shrinkage downward
nodes.hypothesis: The improvement from L2 regularization suggests leaf outputs benefit from shrinkage, but the stronger tested value degraded validation; reducing lambda_l2 to 1.0 may retain generalization while recovering useful signal.

nodes.title: Use slower, longer boosting
nodes.hypothesis: A lower learning rate with a larger boosting budget can improve ranking generalization by producing smoother leaf-output updates while allowing the regularized ranker to reach a better validation optimum.

nodes.title: Tune intermediate L2 regularization
nodes.hypothesis: The tested lambda_l2=2.0 improved substantially, while stronger and weaker regularization degraded; an intermediate value of 2.5 may better balance shrinkage of sparse categorical-history leaves against retaining useful within-user ranking signal.

nodes.title: Add mild L1 regularization
nodes.hypothesis: A small L1 penalty can suppress unstable leaf outputs from sparse high-cardinality history interactions while retaining the useful L2-shrunk ranking signal, improving validation GAUC and nDCG@5.

nodes.title: Add feature subsampling regularization
nodes.hypothesis: Subsampling features at each tree should reduce overfitting from correlated high-cardinality user, item, and history features while preserving enough context to improve validation generalization.

nodes.title: Smooth categorical splits
nodes.hypothesis: Increasing LightGBM categorical smoothing should reduce overfit from sparse user, item, and interaction-history category statistics while preserving robust within-user ranking signal.

nodes.title: Increase numeric histogram resolution
nodes.hypothesis: Increasing max_bin lets LightGBM preserve finer distinctions in continuous recency, duration, and historical-rate features, improving within-user ordering without changing the feature set or ranking objective.

nodes.title: Increase histogram resolution further
nodes.hypothesis: Raising max_bin from 511 to 1023 may preserve finer distinctions in continuous recency and feedback-rate features, improving within-user ordering beyond the current best without changing leakage-safe features.

nodes.title: Use intermediate histogram resolution
nodes.hypothesis: The improvement from max_bin=511 followed by degradation at 1023 suggests an intermediate 767 may preserve useful recency and rate distinctions while avoiding the finer-bin overfitting seen at 1023.

nodes.title: Tune histogram resolution near the current optimum
nodes.hypothesis: The gain from max_bin=767 and degradation at 1023 suggest the optimum may lie slightly below 767; using 640 can retain useful recency and rate distinctions while reducing fine-bin overfitting.

nodes.title: Tune XE-NDCG gradient scaling
nodes.hypothesis: Reducing the XE-NDCG sigmoid scale should soften overly aggressive pairwise gradients from noisy within-user comparisons, improving generalization while preserving the current top-5-focused ranking objective.
